Or people without a sense of smell, etc. Do they get any benefits? What about people who are color blind?
We've all heard that the other senses get stronger to compensate for blindness. What about deafness? Do deaf people develop amazing vision?

In the sense they are more attentive to what they see because that's their main clue as to what is happening? Yes.

The saying depend mostly as to when the deafness/blindness occur : if it's early enough, the brain will rewire itself, giving more processing power to the other senses. But it won't magically make you see or hear better, only make you able to process more of what you already percieve in a given time.

If it happen too late, well, your brain is already wired so to speak, so getting any advantage of what you don't need (anymore) will be harder.
